chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Pray in the Masjid al-Khief, and it is the Masjid of Mina, and it was the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in his era, by the minaret that is in the middle of the Masjid, and above it towards the Qiblah approximately thirty cubits, and to its right, and to its left, and behind it, approximately to that extent.

So investigate that location, and if you are able to make your place of prayer within it, then do so, for indeed a thousand Prophets have prayed in it; and it is named 'al-Khief' because it is elevated from the valley, and whatever is elevated from it is called 'Khief'.

key_terms.أَلْفُ نَبِيٍّ: A thousand prophets, indicating high spiritual status
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The Qiblah, the direction of prayer towards the Kaaba
key_terms.ذِرَاعاً: Cubits, a traditional unit of measurement
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْخَيْفِ: The specific mosque in Mina known as the Elevated Mosque
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the site near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: Where exactly should one pray in Mina according to the tradition of the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Masjid al-Khief in Mina as the preferred prayer site, linking the physical location to the spiritual legacy of a thousand prophets and clarifying the etymology of 'Khief' as an elevated area. It serves as a key juristic reference for Hajj rituals, emphasizing the continuity of prophetic practice and the specific geographical markers that define the sanctity of the prayer space during the pilgrimage.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin IBrahi, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Pray Salaat in the Masjid Al-Khief, and it is a Masjid of Mina, and was a Masjid of Rasool-Allahsaww in hissaww era, by the minaret in the middle of the Masjid and above it up to the Qiblah, approximately thirty cubits; and from its right, and from its left, and behind it (as well) approximate to that’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So investigate that, and if you are able to Pray therein, then do so, for a thousand Prophets<sup>as</sup> have Prayed therein; and rather, it has been named as ‘Al-Khief’ because it is higher from the valley, and whatever is higher from it is called ‘Khief’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

You should perform Salat (prayer) in Masjid al-Khif, it is Masjid of Mina’. The Masjid of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, was near the minaret in the center of the Masjid. Above this place toward al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah) is thirty yards as well as from its right, left and backsides.

If you can perform Salat (prayer) there then do so because one thousand prophets have performed Salat (prayer) there. It is called al-Khif because it is higher than the valley and what is higher is called Khif.’”
